Фудбалски Клуб Шкендија | nickname = ''Balli'' (The Ball) | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1979|8|27}} | ground = [[City Stadium Gostivar]], [[Gostivar]]{{cite web |date=10 June 2026 |title=Шкендија (Т) како домаќин ќе игра во Гостивар, а Шкендија (А) на Чаир! (ФОТО) |url=https://sportsport.mk/2026/06/10/%D1%88%D0%BA%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%B4%D0%B8%D1%98%D0%B0-%D1%82-%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%BA%D0%BE-%D0%B4%D0%BE%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%9C%D0%B8%D0%BD-%D1%9C%D0%B5-%D0%B8%D0%B3%D1%80%D0%B0-%D0%B2%D0%BE-%D0%B3%D0%BE%D1%81/ |access-date=22 July 2026 |website=sportsport.mk}} (temporarily) | capacity = 4,000 | owner = [[Ecolog International]] | chairman = Zamir Dika | mgrtitle = Manager | manager = [[Artim Pollozhani]] | league = [[Macedonian First Football League|Macedonian First League]] | season = [[2025–26 Macedonian First Football League|2025–26]] | position = [[Macedonian First Football League|Macedonian First League]] 2nd of 12 | website = {{URL|kfshkendija.com}} | pattern_la1 = _shkendija2526h | pattern_b1 = _shkendija2526h | pattern_ra1 = _shkendija2526h | pattern_sh1 = _macronshedeco2425br | leftarm1 = 000000 | body1 = FF0000 | rightarm1 = 000000 | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_la2 = _shkendija2223a | pattern_b2 = _shkendija2223a | pattern_ra2 = _shkendija2223a | pattern_sh2 = _macronshedeco2425wb | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF }}'''Klubi i Futbollit Shkëndija''' ([[Macedonian language|Macedonian]]: Фудбалски клуб Шкендија), commonly known as '''Shkëndija''', is a professional football club from [[Tetovo]], [[North Macedonia]]. Founded in 1979 by members of the local Albanian community, the club is closely associated with red-and-black colours and the ultras group [[Ballistët]].{{cite web |title=Historiku |url=https://kfshkendija.com/historiku/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=KF Shkëndija (official) |language=sq}} Shkëndija play home matches at the modern [[Ecolog Arena]] in Tetovo and, since August 2013, have operated under the ownership of the Tetovo-based company [[Ecolog International]].{{cite web |date=1 August 2013 |title=Ecolog takes over Shkendija |url=https://macedonianfootball.com/ecolog-takes-over-shkendija/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=MacedonianFootball.com}} After being dissolved in the early 1980s, the club was re-established in 1992 following [[1991 Macedonian independence referendum|Macedonian independence]] and climbed back through the domestic pyramid, earning a first promotion to the top flight in [[1996–97 Macedonian First Football League|1996–97]].{{cite news |date=8 July 2015 |title=KF Shkëndija v Aberdeen: 11 things you need to know |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/617377/kf-shkendija-v-aberdeen-11-things-know-dons-europa-league-opponents/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |work=Press and Journal}} Shkëndija won their first national championship in the [[2010–11 Macedonian First Football League|2010–11 season]] with 72 points (21–9–3) and lifted the inaugural [[Macedonian Football Supercup]] a few weeks later.{{cite web |date=28 May 2011 |title=Shkendija Tetovo wins the Macedonian First League |url=https://macedonianfootball.com/shkendija-tetovo-wins-the-macedonian-first-league/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=MacedonianFootball.com}}{{cite web |date=24 July 2011 |title=Shkendija lifts the Super Cup |url=https://macedonianfootball.com/shkendija-lifts-the-super-cup/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=MacedonianFootball.com}} Sustained investment in the mid-2010s turned the club into a regular contender; league titles followed in [[2017–18 Macedonian First Football League|2017–18]], [[2018–19 Macedonian First Football League|2018–19]], [[2020–21 Macedonian First Football League|2020–21]] and [[2024–25 Macedonian First Football League|2024–25]].{{cite web |title=1.MFL 2017/18 — Final standings |url=https://macedonianfootball.com/final-standings-first-league-2017-18/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=MacedonianFootball.com}}{{cite web |title=1.MFL 2018/19 — Final standings |url=https://macedonianfootball.com/final-standings-first-league-2018-19/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=MacedonianFootball.com}}{{cite web |date=13 May 2021 |title=Shkëndija win 2020–21 title |url=https://macedonianfootball.com/shkendija-are-champions-2020-21/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=MacedonianFootball.com}}{{cite web |date=13 May 2025 |title=Shkëndija crowned champions 2024–25 |url=https://macedonianfootball.com |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=MacedonianFootball.com}} Internationally, Shkëndija debuted in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League]] qualifiers and have twice reached the [[UEFA Europa League]] play-off round (2016–17, 2017–18), losing to [[K.A.A. Gent|Gent]] and [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] respectively.{{cite web |date=19 July 2011 |title=Polished Partizan prevail against Shkëndija |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea66a5b972c-82850a595e6d-1000--polished-partizan-prevail-against-shkendija/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=UEFA.com}}{{cite web |date=25 August 2016 |title=Shkëndija 0–4 Gent — play-off 2nd leg |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2020473--shkendija-vs-gent/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=UEFA.com}}{{cite web |date=17 August 2017 |title=Milan 6–0 Shkëndija — play-off 1st leg |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2021952--milan-vs-shkendija/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=UEFA.com}} Their deepest [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] run came in [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|2018–19]], eliminating [[The New Saints F.C.|The New Saints]] and [[FC Sheriff Tiraspol|Sheriff]] before falling to [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Salzburg]] in Q3 and then to [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] in the Europa League play-off.{{cite web |date=8 August 2018 |title=Salzburg 3–0 Shkëndija — UCL Q3 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2025308--salzburg-vs-shkendija/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=UEFA.com}}{{cite web |date=23 August 2018 |title=Rosenborg 3–1 Shkëndija — UEL play-off |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2025420--rosenborg-vs-shkendija/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=UEFA.com}} In the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|2020–21]] Q3 they hosted [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in Skopje (1–3), a match preceded by a goalframe measurement controversy that led to the replacement of undersized posts.{{cite web |date=24 September 2020 |title=Shkëndija 1–3 Tottenham — match centre |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2030385--shkendija-vs-tottenham/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=UEFA.com}}{{cite news |date=24 September 2020 |title=Harry Kane helps Tottenham past Shkëndija after goalpost controversy |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/sep/24/shkendija-tottenham-europa-league-qualifier-match-report |access-date=1 August 2025 |work=The Guardian}} In [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|2025–26]] qualifying, Shkëndija beat [[The New Saints F.C.|The New Saints]] in Q1 and upset [[FCSB]] in Q2 (3–1 agg.) to reach Q3.{{cite web |title=FCSB vs Shkëndija — match centre |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2045390--fcsb-vs-shkendija/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=UEFA.com}} Shkëndija's principal rivalry is the Tetovo derby with [[FK Teteks]], which has produced several high-risk fixtures and the [[2012–13 Macedonian Football Cup|2013]] cup final abandonment; derbies are also contested with [[FK Renova]], [[FK Vardar]], and [[KF Shkupi]].{{cite web |title=Macedonian derbies — Derby of Tetovo |url=https://macedonianfootball.com/macedonian-derbies/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=MacedonianFootball.com}}{{cite news |date=23 May 2013 |title=Macedonia cup final abandoned after crowd trouble |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/macedonia-cup-final-abandoned-after-crowd-trouble-2013-05-23/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |work=Reuters}}{{cite web |date=9 November 2022 |title=Shkupi–Shkëndija quarter-final abandoned — FFM awards 3–0 |url=https://ffm.mk/en/competition-commission-official-victory-for-fc-shkendija-and-suspension-at-the-stadium-of-fc-shkupi |access-date=1 August 2025 |website=FFM.mk}}"}}
